Based on the provided income statement, the company demonstrates a healthy financial position. The gross profit margin is 50% ($300,000 gross profit), indicating strong pricing power or cost control on goods sold. Operating expenses are well-managed at 50% of gross profit, resulting in a solid operating income of $150,000. After accounting for interest and taxes, the company retains a net income of $100,000, which represents a net profit margin of approximately 33.3% (assuming revenue was $300,000 + operating expenses, or more accurately, if we assume Gross Profit is Revenue minus COGS, we need Revenue to calculate exact margins, but the absolute net income is positive and substantial). The ability to cover interest expenses and taxes while still generating significant net income suggests good liquidity and solvency.
